body: I've implemented and tested a fix in which I call a new splitOnce() routine in StringUtil() which basically behaves like an optimized String.split(delim, 2).  I figure that there may be other places where a single split is desired.  I created unit tests for splitOnce() and updated testBinaryStreamUpload by putting a "=" char in the boundary.  "mvn test" is clean.  Should I bother to submit?

Hmmn I believe in this case, we only need to get the substring. No need to get the first part.
I believe using indexOf and substring shall be more efficient in this case than split(delim, 2) since we don't need the first part... Don't you think ?
However I agree that in other part of Netty, such a splitOnce could be useful.
I will try on my side to propose something but you can of course propose something too !

issue.title: Backport http post request decoder 4.1 to 4.0 + "=" Boundary fix

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Fix "=" character in HttpPostRequestDecoder
 Backport 4.1 to 4.0 on HttpPostRequestDecoder

Motivation:
4.0 was not modified in the same time than 4.1 while the difference was limited and was revealed in issue #2886 .
Issue #3004 shows that "=" character was not supported as it should in the HttpPostRequestDecoder in form-data boundary.

Modifications:
Backport of 4.1
Add 2 methods in StringUtil
- splitInTwo: String split with a 2 parts only (to prevent multiple '=' to be source of extra split while not needed)
- afterDelim: String part after delimiter (since first part is not needed)
  Use those methods in HttpPostRequestDecoder.
  Change and the HttpPostRequestDecoderTest to check using a boundary beginning with "=".

Results:
Backport done (Issue #2886 fix)
The fix implies more stability and fix the issue #3004 .
